about.title: Integration guide
about.intro: CP OAuth supports the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with a client secret, PKCE, or both.

flow.title: Authorization code flow
flow.step1: Redirect the user to /oauth/authorize with your client ID, registered callback URI and requested scopes. Include state to verify the callback.
flow.step2: The user reviews the requested access and chooses whether to approve it.
flow.step3: On approval, your callback receives an authorization code. Validate the returned state before continuing.
flow.step4: Exchange the single-use code for an access token and refresh token at POST /api/oauth/token.
flow.step5: Call GET /api/oauth/userinfo with the Bearer access token to read the data covered by the granted scopes.
flow.step6: Refresh at POST /api/oauth/token with grant_type=refresh_token. Omit client_secret only if the initial PKCE code exchange omitted it.

endpoints.title: API endpoints
endpoints.authorize_desc: Starts the consent flow. The callback URI must exactly match a registered URI: HTTPS, or HTTP on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. A user can deny access without signing in; the callback receives access_denied and the original state.
endpoints.token_desc: Accepts authorization_code and rotating refresh_token grants as JSON or URL-encoded scalar form fields. Public PKCE grants must omit client_secret entirely; empty or incorrect secrets are rejected. A refresh request may narrow the granted scopes, but cannot add scopes.
endpoints.userinfo_desc: Returns only the user data covered by the granted scopes.
endpoints.revoke_desc: Revokes your application's access or refresh token (RFC 7009). Secret authentication follows the original grant. Revoking a refresh token also invalidates all access tokens for that user and application. A valid request returns 200 for an unknown token; token_type_hint only affects lookup order.
endpoints.token_lifetime: Access tokens expire after 1 hour; refresh tokens expire after 30 days. Save both new tokens returned by each refresh.

scopes.title: Permission scopes
scopes.description: Request a non-empty set of only the scopes your application needs. The openid scope is optional. The userinfo response follows stored granted scopes, independently of public-profile privacy settings.
scopes.openid: User ID (sub only; no ID token)
scopes.profile: Username, display name, avatar URL and bio
scopes.cp_linked: All linked platform accounts (platform, UID and username)
scopes.cp_summary: Rating, contest count and rank from Clist.by for accounts that exactly match locally linked identities
scopes.cp_details: Up to 200 recent rated contest changes from Clist.by for accounts that exactly match locally linked identities

pkce.title: PKCE
pkce.description: Public applications can exchange authorization codes using PKCE without a client secret. Always send code_verifier when exchanging a PKCE code.
pkce.exchange_title: Exchange a code without a secret
pkce.verifier_rules: The verifier must be 43–128 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore, tilde or hyphen. An S256 challenge is a 43-character base64url SHA-256 hash. The plain method is also supported and is the default when the method is omitted.
pkce.grant_rule: When the initial PKCE exchange omits the secret, refresh and revoke requests for that grant can also omit it. Grants created before the migration still require a secret until the user authorizes again.

card.title: User profile card
card.description: Embed an SVG card of a user's public platform accounts in a GitHub README or blog. The card shows only accounts the user has made public.
card.params: Parameters: width (default 480, range 300–800), theme (light or dark, default light), lang (en/zh/ja, default en).

about.guide_intro: Register an application and use OAuth 2.0 to request access to user data.
about.cookie_boundary: CP OAuth's own pages use HttpOnly session cookies and CSRF protection. Your integration uses grant credentials for token exchange and revocation, and a Bearer access token for userinfo. Do not use or forward the site's session cookie.

create.title: Register an application
create.description: In the developer workspace, enter an application name and exact callback URIs, then choose whether approval requires a verified email. Callbacks must use HTTPS; HTTP is allowed only on loopback addresses for local development. The client secret is shown once after creation. Save it securely if your server will use it.

credentials.title: Server-side authentication
credentials.description: Keep client_secret on your server, not in browser code. Client secret authentication can be used with or without PKCE. If the authorization request used PKCE, include code_verifier in the code exchange.
credentials.grant_rule: If the initial code exchange includes a secret, refresh and revoke requests for that grant must also include the client secret. Missing, empty or incorrect secrets are rejected.

about.protocol_note: This is not a full OpenID Connect provider. The openid scope returns a user ID, not an ID token; no JWKS endpoint is published.
